articles.summary: A bipartisan House trio outlined a sweeping new artificial intelligence proposal that would require companies to adhere to minimum federal safety standards and disclose any lapses while clarifying where liability lies for foreseeable injuries tied to the technology. articles.title: US AI Chip Crackdown Shakes Supply Chains
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department announced stricter export controls on AI chips, explicitly targeting data centers serving Chinese firms to close a loophole in prior restrictions. The move follows reports that nearly 880,000 AI chips were approved for export to China earlier this month. Nvidia confirmed it would halt sales of its most advanced chips to China, while Alibaba revised its cloud growth outlook downward citing the curbs as a direct constraint.

articles.summary: Oil gained late in trading as worries about possible renewed attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran and holiday short-covering lifted prices. Brent settled at 92.57 dollars a barrel, up 0.64 percent, while WTI finished at 83.98. Both benchmarks were on track for a third straight weekly decline as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels. The Houthis warned of attacks on Saudi Red Sea ports and two tankers hit naval mines in the strait.

articles.title: Bluenami green energy boost only reaches so far
articles.summary: Fighting climate change just got easier in the United States after Democratic midterm successes ousted key climate-sceptic Republican lawmakers and voters expressed unease over power-hungry AI data centres. Shares in American cleantech companies jumped 5 percent or more. But the green energy boost will only reach so far: the US imposed tariffs of between 50 and 248 percent on clean tech from China, and renewables already accounted for more than 90 percent of energy added to the US system last year.

articles.title: China Unlikely to Fulfill 17 Billion US Ag Purchase Pledge This Year
articles.summary: China looks unlikely to fulfill a pledge to buy billions of dollars in US farm products in 2026 as leaders of the two nations prepare for their third meeting this year. The two sides agreed in September to lower tariffs on a slew of farm products, but nearly two months later those cuts are still pending.
